messages:
maya: heads-up — after today's runtime roll (canary->prod) we're seeing p99 decode latency up ~25% on host-side paths (tokenize + parse). noticed on several routes. :eyes:
ci-bot: deploy-bot: runtime-service@v2.14.3 -> prod (canary promoted) at 2026-03-19T18:00:12Z
raj: any flamegraphs yet?
maya: quick perf from a repro run shows CPU time dominated by host_tokenizer::split and parse::proto_unmarshal. also lots of tiny writev syscalls. snippet:
```
# top samples (sampled)
host_tokenizer::split 34.2%
parse::proto_unmarshal 21.8%
http2::frame_parse 9.5%
kv_cache::lookup 8.3%
writev 7.1%
other 19.1%
```
olga: can you paste the alloc profile? the tokenizer change we merged last week allocs a lot of 64B buffers, might explain churn. :thinking_face:
maya: allocs are high — many short-lived 64B/128B buffers. perf record snippet + commands I used:
```
perf record -F 99 -a -- sleep 30
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > f.svg
```
sam: i also noticed kvcache hot-shard misses went up after we bumped the minibatch hints. kernel selection might be flipping to a slower path for short sequences. did the canary change batching heuristic?
raj: i rolled a change yesterday that tightened minibatch flush timeout from 6ms -> 2ms to reduce p50 for short requests. that could increase syscall frequency and reduce amortized batching.
maya: repro steps i used: send 1000 short requests (5–30 tokens) concurrently via http/gRPC gateway. p99 regresses consistently. microbenchmark numbers:
```
requests=1000 concurrency=64
baseline(v2.14.2): p50=18ms p95=42ms p99=78ms
v2.14.3:             p50=16ms p95=48ms p99=98ms
```
olga: tail worse even if median improved. my hypothesis: lower flush timeout cuts batching, increasing syscall/writev overhead and causing KV cache thrash (more lookups per token). suggest trying: revert timeout, add route-level batch_hints, and enable writev coalescing in host proxy.
sam: +1. also seeing http2 HPACK decode cost on host for many small streams. can we try connection reuse / fewer streams per connection?
maya: i pushed a small experiment branch `maya/coalesce-writev-smoke` that coalesces small writes in proxy. can run perf with it against canary.
raj: i'll repro with kvcache tracing and kernel-selection debug flags on prod-canary to see if model kernel flips correlate with short seq distribution. @olga can you run jemalloc stats + flame for the same window?
olga: on it — running jemalloc.bgstats and a short flame capture now, will upload.
ci-bot: incident-bot: diagnostics bundle uploaded: https://internal.redwood/diag/6112223333 (includes perf/flame, alloc traces, kvcache counters)
maya: :thumbsup: i'll collect traces from the branch + canary, and if we confirm tail regression caused by the timeout change we'll rollback the flush change for the next hour window. p99 SLOs > product priority.
sam: agree — if rollback necessary, coordinate with release team at 19:30 UTC.
raj: i'll post kvcache traces and kernel-selection logs in this thread when ready.
maya: thanks all, will update in ~30m with flame + a proposed revert PR link.
